humanities_role_explanation: Jokes and puns (SemEval-2017 Task 7, Context-Situated Puns, ExplainTheJoke) supply the items, but the paper tests a general prompting method (text+TTS audio) for explanation quality rather than disciplinary competence in a humanities field.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Jokes are given as text plus a synthetic spoken version generated with OpenAI tts-1-hd; both are passed to Gemini-1.5-Flash in a single prompt (or separately then aggregated). Output is text.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Pun detection (pun vs non-pun) and free-text humor explanation, judged pairwise by an LLM against human explanations or between prompting strategies. Explanation of wordplay/phonetic ambiguity maps to interpretation and generation.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to humor/pun explanation; no new benchmark, it is a prompting study on three existing datasets.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Gemini-1.5-Flash generates explanations; GPT-4o is the judge.

quantitative_metrics.note: Pairwise win rate and tie rate from LLM-as-judge, position-swap averaged.

summary: The paper proposes multimodal prompting for humor explanation, supplying an LLM with both the text and TTS-generated audio of a joke. Evaluated on SemEval-2017 Task 7, Context-Situated Puns and ExplainTheJoke with an LLM judge, audio improves win rates across all datasets. Ablations and logit analysis support that audio preserves phonetic ambiguity.
key_findings: On SemEval, audio raises win rate vs human explanations from 47.76 to 51.74 (heterographs) and 68.89 to 72.59 (homographs). Gains on Context-Situated Puns and ExplainTheJoke are also positive (ExplainTheJoke 12.81 vs 15.44). Audio-only is much worse (25.50 heterograph, 55.86 homograph). Voice choice has no significant effect.
dataset_size: SemEval 2017 Task 7: 810 homographic + 647 heterographic puns + 1077 non-puns; Context-Situated Puns: 821 + 1739 puns; ExplainTheJoke: 350 jokes (total 5444).
gold_upstream: SemEval-2017 Task 7 (Miller et al., 2017): human annotations of pun-word and meanings plus human explanations; production not further described in this paper. Also Context-Situated Puns (Sun et al., 2022) and ExplainTheJoke (theblackcat102).
facets_explanation: Reference material is reused from existing datasets: SemEval human annotations and explanations, Context-Situated Puns annotations, and ExplainTheJoke human explanations (summarized by GPT). Scoring is by a GPT-4o pairwise judge given the annotations, not key matching. Explaining jokes requires world/linguistic knowledge beyond the surface text.
results_explanation: Best headline is the SemEval homograph win rate versus human explanations, 'with audio 72.59' (Table 1). The largest input-representation gap is text+audio vs audio-only on heterographs in Table 4: 'Our System 51.74' vs 'No text, Audio Only 25.50', about 26 points; reported as 30 is an overstatement, see note: homograph gap is 72.59 vs 55.86 = 17. No human baseline score is reported; the human explanations are the comparison reference only.
